meta.title: Impact
meta.description: How Friends of Animals will count what it does, and what it will publish.

hero.title: What we count, and how we count it
hero.lead: Kindness is hard to measure. What we can count honestly is who took part, where, and what came of it. This page shows those numbers and the rules behind them.
hero.easy: We count the children who take part and the schools that join. We only show numbers we can check.
hero.photoCaption: A puppy asks its mother to play

method.title: How we count
method.lead: Each number comes straight from our records, not from estimates. These are the rules.
method.caption: What each number means

participants.name: Children and young people
participants.def: Each person with at least one confirmed registration, counted once however many competitions they enter.

institutions.name: Schools and institutions
institutions.def: Verified schools and institutions with at least one confirmed registration.

competitions.name: Competitions
competitions.def: Competitions whose results have been published.

statesReached.name: States and union territories
statesReached.def: States and union territories where at least one counted participant lives.

artworksShowcased.name: Works shown in public
artworksShowcased.def: Works live in the public gallery, shown with consent.

funds.name: Money raised
funds.def: Donations net of refunds in the latest published financial year, from the same reconciled ledger as the transparency page.

rules.title: The rules
rules.small: Numbers under 10 are not shown, so no one can work out who took part from a small count.
rules.round: Bigger numbers are rounded down to the nearest ten, with a plus: 1,249 becomes 1,240+.
rules.offline: If a number includes work done offline, such as paper entries, we say so next to it.
rules.asOf: Every number carries the date it was counted.
rules.targets: We never show our targets as if they were results.
